Note: Currently have 63 hours in game, and am grinding to beat the Pyro incursion.

Edit: Decided to drop the game after I realized that, on top of the grind you can pay to bypass, you have to pay to unlock additional Descendant slots after 10. I'm at 6. I HAVE basically beat the game now, having completed the main story line and Bunny's quest line.

I wish there was a "neutral" option, as there are serious negatives attached to this game. Specifically, monetization. However, the game itself is actually quite engaging. But the monetization cannot be overlooked, so I'm going with no.

Don't go into it thinking you're getting a third person shooter experience, this is more an RPG with a third person shooter skin. It's fun to TFD's various systems to min-max your character, and eventually turn them into a monster. If you're looking for a third person shooter, look elsewhere.

That said, all of these systems are time gated, and while you can do pretty much everything mechanical wise by grinding a bit, all of these systems have a very apparent end goal of tempting you to bypass time gates of some sort. And the stuff isn't fairly priced either, some skins or descendants are approaching $100 to buy them out right.

If you are weak against FOMO or other sketchier mechanics, avoid this like the plague.

Otherwise, this can be a good distraction for a bit.

I'm probably going to play this until some mechanic is introduced that prevents me from progressing without selling my liver. I MAY drop $40 or so for a "buying the game" equivalent purchase in the future, if I find myself spending 200+ hours in game. I suppose the devs have earned it at that point. But nothing more.

A cash-shop wrapped in a game that borrows heavily from titles like Warframe and Destiny without bringing much new to the table by itself. Like many others already stated the weapon- and character upgrade system for instance is a 1:1 copy of the one used in Warframe. Even the repeatable missions have a very similar feel to the ones in Warframe. Again, without any new spin or re-imagination, just a blatant copy.

The core gameplay mechanics and overall visual presentation are serviceable - a notable exception would be the lackluster voice "acting". Overall it feels void of interesting activities and even barebones in some parts aswell - Large areas where absolutely nothing happens. The instanced boss-battles are pretty fun though and in my opinion the only small highlight in the game.

My advice would be not to put any money into this as of yet because I have a creeping suspicion that this game won't survive another year or so. I'd be happy if proven wrong.

I'll get the bad out of the way first so I can tell you why I gave this a thumbs up.

YES this game is a nexon game so the item shop pricing is pretty silly. It's also pretty obvious that the game's drop rates are lowish to inflate progression. Does this mean you shouldn't play it? No. Why? The game is fun. Genuinely.

The shooting feels good, at the time of writing this, its easy to find people to play with to clear missions and the character designs are pretty great! If you are a fan of looter shooter this one is great. I would recommend this game to others who aren't credit card happy and want a grindy shooter to play. You can certainly buy character straight out, but why? Isn't the point of playing to unlock these things? Atleast from my experience, any game i outright buy content I can play for, i end up dropping it because the shiny thing I wanted is gone. 

Give it a try, if you don't like it after the first 5-10 hours, drop it.

After playing 30+ hours of the game so far, I feel confident on giving a review for the game now. This was a game that was on my radar off and on since it was announced. After hearing that this game would be a looter shooter, it peaked my interest even more so it made me even more excited. Then when the game came out as F2P, I realized that I had to get it. So here is my opinion.

Personally, I don't know how this game is getting a "Mixed" rating where most of the negative reviews are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the pay to win aspects. Apart from the cosmetic costumes, everything or almost everything is obtainable in game thru grinding, and as someone that enjoyed varying other looter shooters such as Borderlands, Division, etc... I never mind a little grind since I know I can work toward something. I also know that there are those people who just don't have much time on their hands and don't mind spending a few dollars to get it faster. Nothing is wrong w/ that since this game (I think) is purely 4 player co op. So it's honestly super helpful when I get someone with a stronger char to help me clear the story faster. I am working on unlocking a couple of other chars.

The story is alright for what it is, but I def mainly play the game for the looter shooter aspect, which is very nice in my opinion. Some of the missions (like the platforming ones) def can make you upset (unless you are more skilled unlike me lol) but all in all, as a free game it's not like you'd have to pay anything just to try it out so I would def recommend it

Well, honestly, I am very, very disappointed and upset with this project.
In short, this game is a mix of Destiny and Warframe, where they tried to create an even better game, but as you can see, they didn’t find success. I’m the guy who participated in the last two tests of this game and also played a lot of Warframe (more than 5 years), even tried Destiny but didn’t like it.
From the start, as I said, I played the test, and if not mentioning the story (which is boring or even stupid in some places), the first three locations are good and look cool (my favorite is the third, very beautiful). It was also the last map in the test that I saw (limit), and they did it very well with good enemies and good missions (almost good, but more on that later).
BUT, after, from location to location, it gets worse and worse. People who play Warframe will understand me about "Eximus" (in that game, they are guys with some passive, again PASSIVE ability, and more health, which is even worse as they can have not only one of those abilities). I will use that name for them because I don’t know another, thanks.
Well, yeah, those guys will infiltrate your mission more and more as you go further in hard zones... and honestly, I’m not that much against them, but everything has a limit. When one enemy with the ability to suck your "mana" AND block abilities because he’s close enough has an impenetrable sphere shield that also covers others if you’re not inside (which also means very fast death if you’re not tanky enough or have some good heavy weapon), or worse, when they have one/two weak point shields (any other part than this weak point will absorb everything except abilities) and he’s not alone; as a bonus, he has friends with some other or the same ability. I saw two Eximus with Sphere shields and after that three 1-point guys... good luck killing that while you’re also struggling to kill normal mobs.

Descendants:
 Beautiful... but Bunny... come on, "prime" Bunny is kind of too much; she’s almost nude, and I’m a guy, but still, it’s too much. Also, farming some descendants is kind of annoying but okay. The descendants themselves are okay... well, please give Blair his ability back -_-. Otherwise, they are okay; they’re different, and almost all of them are useful. Of course, there’s the best and worst, but you can complete your story using your main/first Descendant.
Weapons: Okay, you can farm all weapons from mobs (but not the ones you need to craft), and you also can’t change them as you want. Second stats are random when you get them and depend on the level of the weapon (after you upgrade it, you’ll need to reroll stats using a craftable item, which honestly, I don’t find any problem with, but if you overuse it, then sorry, you’ll need to wait and farm for resources). On the other hand, you will definitely find a weapon you like.
Reactors & Modules (under Reactor in inventory menu): Hard to get, and speaking about Reactors (they give additional/main ability power and, as I found out not so long ago, some stats bonus like modules or weapons), they have some conditions for the bonus (+40%) where you need to use a specific weapon or weapon and gold reactor. You need to use a special GOLD weapon, and the game doesn’t care if you have it or not; you just can’t, and it’s really hard when you have the reactor but don’t have the weapon. And now purple is better (because of the 40% bonus).
--Mods:
 It’s hard; you can’t easily increase capacity, and you need all mods to be good so you won’t die and can deal some damage too. In the end, it’s okay; you feel like in Warframe but also somehow different and cool. If you like doing stuff like calculating stats and creating your OP Descendant, go ahead ;-).
Graphics: It’s beautiful, sometimes laggy, buggy, and all that, but not that bad. You’d probably like to stay and look around for some time just because of how beautiful it is. BUT, optimization is not great. Not like I have a potato PC, but still, sometimes it freezes and lags (I don’t know if it’s a host problem or what; in Warframe, if the host has bad internet, then everyone lags). That’s why don’t try playing on a potato... yet, wait for a patch :-) .
Well, now the most painful part for me:

--Stats:
 Oh hell, I spent hours just not dying. They used stupid logic from Warframe (which everyone thinks is the one that kills armor), but again limits....80% is the max for both armor and element defense (the additional defense that takes part of element damage, very useful against bosses, must have minimum gap). For ARMOR, again, it may have logic in it, but how the heck am I supposed to know when I reach a d*mn limit? I spent hours dying because I thought I reached the 80% limit, but no, I found out that 10k armor is NOT ENOUGH to not just die from trash mobs. On the other hand, enemy mods are tanky and deal a lot of damage. Also, some small problems with stats as you often must search where it is, and you can’t find the "nude" stats of your Descendant (or I’m just blind; if you found them, tell me (-_-) ).

-Multiplayer and Balance:
Up to 3 locations, you’re good, after that, you’re a useless piece of sh*t who will die from a number of small fries who will definitely destroy your shield and health just because you hesitated for 1 millisecond or did something wrong... or you’re just alone... yeah, they don’t really have a balance for solo missions if you’re going through the main campaign. You’ll need to wait an endless time to just finish a local mission and go further -_-

Balance: 
Again, not the problem of the player, more or less, it’s okay, but the enemy... well, burn my as as hell. Let’s be honest, it’s not new that if an enemy guides you and shoots straight at you, that would be the easiest way, and all you need is accuracy for bullets. BUT when they did that, they forgot they added a Laser... a dmn Laser. Again, the enemy guides you; now, what do you think is the miss chance? Correct 0.5% (0.5% is just because sometimes they miss). And again, it’s not like they have a one-shot option like a normal projectile, but you will burn because the enemy who has this option is bulky and sometimes has a status effect you didn’t have time to react to. Worse, it will burn you until you find some cover... if you have one, of course, if not, you’re doomed. Oh yeah, another type of "Eximus" guy is the one who creates status damage balls, and the fun fact is you can’t destroy it in the creation phase, only after it’s fully created and gives the first damage. This means you need to run out of this area and then destroy it. To be honest, 1 is not a problem, 2... a little bit, 4... well, you have a problem now, and they may be created close to one another. Oh yeah, also if you go down, they will LITERALLY SPAWN ON YOU TOO. I once died just because I had 3 of them spawning one after another on me, which is why my team didn’t revive me, and also damage kills you faster.
Customization: Painting has a limited amount, which means you can’t just have one opened paint and use it as you want; no, you have a limited amount of it. Also, honestly, colors here are bad. Small amount and don’t look as cool as you wish.

Also not very understandable why there is a Russian language after what they did, and seeing that all countries with knowledge of it prefer not to use it!!

Also, thank you if you read all of this and liked it. 

Summary:
The game, while visually appealing and initially promising, suffers from significant issues such as poorly balanced enemies, problematic mechanics, unoptimized performance, and limited customization options. The design of certain features, like the Eximus units and weapon stats, creates frustration rather than challenge. Additionally, the multiplayer experience is hindered by imbalanced solo missions and a lack of proper matchmaking. Despite these flaws, the game has potential if addressed properly.

I first started playing the game when it came out, maybe 1 of 2 weeks after the release.. Lepic is my first Descendant.

The visuals are stunning. The ambience speaks to me. Gunplay is precise and snappy, with a controller, yeah peasant me! The latency/lags are not impacting the gameplay. The story mode is intriguing. I felt comfortable with the universe and I wanted to complet the challenges.

I purchased a 66$ CAD coins bundle after maybe 50 hours of gameplay in. It was for the battle passes and for minors cosmetics, like hair styles and colours.

The gruesome grinding time for the ending contents came and it was maniac sometimes. It was the 5 minutes cooldown with Sheeran stealth missions, the low rate lottery RNG drops and the huge difficulty spikes for some contents (on my part XD), but I kept playing, always pushing forward.

After somes updates, the game became more and more bearable for ''casuals'' like myself. The grinding was not so much repetitive, after a while..

I've spent so much fun time with Bunny and Thunder Cage at the beginning. She's a fast and skill-full Descendant! I would I've so much like to have different skill colours: imagine crimson lightnings everywhere with Bunny! Please Devs! make it happen!

Freyna was and still an awesome skill based Descendant. I is so much fun seeing those puddles of poison spreading everywhere!

The next Descendant the game gave me another chance to invest in was Ines! My best character so far. Very fast mobber and still reliable vs end game contents. I felt powerful, smart with my choices. The grinding was not so much of a hassle for a while. 

After reaching 19MR, I was not so much interested in grinding for the other Descendants and guns. When you have to return on Normal Kingston for blue guns...

At the time of writing (09-16-2025), I have a 14 Catalyts Nell and a 10C Ult Luna at maybe lvl 28 Arche Tuning, MR25. They are also very interesting in they own style. 

The next new content will arrived on October 1st 2025: the Reactors will no longer be needing the gun matching requirement for the 160% skill boost... yeah! You'll be able to dismantled Anamorphous materials in Albion! Yeahhh.... Too late for me.

It just, I no longer desire to give so much of my time to play this game. It was fun while it lasted..

For the moment, I'll leave all my Descendants in the White Lodge, to let them have their own moments surrounded by the trippy ambiance, in silence.
